issues.message: Only 23 blocks: too bare for a common (at least 50). Carlton wants more detail, not less.

notes.artefacts: cobblestone_wall posts without properties render as '?'

visual.summary: Well level 1: a 3 x 3 cobblestone ring with a slab lid; too small and plain, and the wall posts show as placeholder blocks.
problems: Far too small and bare for the kingdom's water source (23 to 28 blocks): build a 5 x 5 well with a raised two-course stone basin, posts, a windlass beam with a rope or chain and a proper roof.
The cobblestone wall posts have no connection properties and show as "?" placeholder blocks; use log posts instead.
The flat oak slab lid reads as a box: give it a steep gable roof with dark eaves and ridge.
Give each level its own extras (a trough and a bucket barrel at level 2, bushes, flowers and moss at level 3).

notes.roof: steep and well trimmed, but far too big for the small basin

visual.summary: Well level 1: now a real well with posts, windlass and a steep roof, but the roof dwarfs the small 3 x 3 basin.
problems: The roof is two blocks wider than the 3 x 3 basin on every side, so the well looks top-heavy (a mushroom): widen the basin to 5 x 5 under the same kind of roof.
Level 1 has no life at all; fine for a first level, but the levels above should keep adding plants and props.

visual.summary: Well level 1: a 5 x 5 mossy cobblestone basin with dark oak posts, a windlass and chain under a steep two-tone gable roof; plain but clearly a well.
problems: No plants or props yet at this level; the levels above add them.
The full dark plank ridge reads a little heavy; a slab ridge would be lighter.

visual.summary: Smaller and round now, as Carlton asked: a 5 x 5 octagon basin with stair-rounded corners, two dark oak posts and a beam with a chain. Still very bare at this level.
problems: Carlton asked for more detail on all levels: give L1 a bucket (cauldron) or barrel beside the basin, a lantern on a post, a stone step in front

From the front a dark oak post stands right in the middle of the basin and rises above the ridge, hiding the well: put the two posts on the left and right of the basin with the windlass axle between them, or turn the roof so the posts are at the sides
